key_insight: iLoRA introduces a novel Bayesian framework for low-rank adaptation that simultaneously learns prediction and latent interaction structures in microbiome diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: The framework enhances the diagnostic accuracy of disease states by considering both microbial abundance and interactions between microbes.
method: Infers a latent interaction graph from input data.
Generates input-conditioned LoRA updates based on the interaction graph.
Evaluates performance in interactive QA and multi-cohort IBD diagnosis settings.
evidence_signal: iLoRA shows improvements over existing LoRA and Bayesian adaptation methods, aligning graph recovery with human annotations.
watch_item: The moderate overhead of graph-branching may impact computational efficiency.
paper_title: iLoRA: Bayesian Low-Rank Adaptation with Latent Interaction Graphs for Microbiome Diagnosis
